claim: IQSec1 activates both Arf5 and Arf6 in HeLa cells.

claim: Arf6 has been shown to act at the plasma membrane and in endosomal recycling pathways.

evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Knockdown of Arf6 in MDA-MB-231 cells did not phenocopy IQSec1 knockdown.
source: As we had observed in Hela cells (Moravec et al., 2012), knockdown of Arf6 in MDA-MB-231 cells did not phenocopy IQSec1 knockdown; Arf6-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells were actually less well spread than controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).

claim: Arf6-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells were less well spread than controls.
source: As we had observed in Hela cells (Moravec et al., 2012), knockdown of Arf6 in MDA-MB-231 cells did not phenocopy IQSec1 knockdown; Arf6-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells were actually less well spread than controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: Depletion of Arf5 in MDA-MB-231 cells leads to dramatic cell flattening.
source: Conversely, depletion of Arf5 in these cells led to dramatic cell flattening (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C), a significant increase in focal adhesion area (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) with higher β1-integrin content (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), and reduced disassembly rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Depletion of Arf5 leads to a significant increase in focal adhesion area.
source: Conversely, depletion of Arf5 in these cells led to dramatic cell flattening (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C), a significant increase in focal adhesion area (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) with higher β1-integrin content (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), and reduced disassembly rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Depletion of Arf5 leads to higher β1-integrin content in focal adhesions.
source: Conversely, depletion of Arf5 in these cells led to dramatic cell flattening (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C), a significant increase in focal adhesion area (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) with higher β1-integrin content (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), and reduced disassembly rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Depletion of Arf5 leads to reduced disassembly rate.
source: Conversely, depletion of Arf5 in these cells led to dramatic cell flattening (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C), a significant increase in focal adhesion area (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) with higher β1-integrin content (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), and reduced disassembly rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Similar increases in focal adhesion area were observed in HT1080 cells upon Arf5 depletion.
source: Similar increases in focal adhesion area were observed in HT1080 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Arf5 but not Arf6 is essential for focal adhesion turnover.
source: Together, these results strongly suggest that Arf5 but not Arf6 is essential for focal adhesion turnover.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings in the study.

claim: Expression of rapid cycling Arf6 failed to restore FA turnover in IQSec1-depleted cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, expression of rapid cycling Arf6 failed to restore FA turnover in IQSec1-depleted cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression of rapid cycling Arf5 largely restored adhesion turnover in IQSec1-depleted cells.
source: In contrast, expression of rapid cycling Arf5 largely restored adhesion turnover (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Knockdown of Arf5 substantially impairs migration in the matrigel migration assay.
source: Like IQSec1, knockdown of Arf5 substantially impaired migration in the matrigel migration assay (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Activation of Arf5, not Arf6, by IQSec1 mediates focal adhesion disassembly in migrating cells.
source: Together, these data suggest that activation of Arf5, not Arf6, by IQSec1 mediates focal adhesion disassembly in migrating cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings in the study.

claim: Thapsigargin-induced calcium influx increased active Arf5 by ~50% over basal levels in cells expressing WT IQSec1.
source: As shown in Figure 2D - E, thapsigargin-induced calcium influx increased active Arf5 by ~50% over basal levels in cells expressing WT IQSec1, whereas cells expressing the IQSec1 E606K mutant did not show a significant change in active Arf5 levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2D-E.

claim: Cells expressing the IQSec1 E606K mutant did not show a significant change in active Arf5 levels after thapsigargin treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 2D - E, thapsigargin-induced calcium influx increased active Arf5 by ~50% over basal levels in cells expressing WT IQSec1, whereas cells expressing the IQSec1 E606K mutant did not show a significant change in active Arf5 levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2D-E.

claim: Arf5 activation is inhibited by ~60% by the selective Orai1 channel blocker, BTP2.
source: In contrast, Arf5 activation is inhibited by ~60% by the selective Orai1 channel blocker, BTP2 (Figure 2F–G), indicating that Arf5 activation is indeed modulated by calcium influx.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2F-G.

claim: Residual Arf5 activity in the presence of BTP2 represents Arf5 in the early secretory pathway, where it is activated by a different GEF, GBF1.
source: Residual activity in the presence of BTP2 presumably represents Arf5 in the early secretory pathway, where it is activated by a different GEF, GBF1 (Chun et al., 2008; Claude et al., 1999; Volpicelli-Daley et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings based on established knowledge about Arf5 and GBF1.

claim: An increase in FA size was observed in MDA-MB-231 cells depleted of STIM1.
source: As expected, we also observed an increase in FA size in MDA-MB-231 cells depleted of STIM1 (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: No significant migration was observed out of spheroids generated from STIM1 depleted cells in 3D collagen gels.
source: Similarly, no significant migration was observed out of spheroids generated from STIM1 depleted cells in 3D collagen gels (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: GFP-STIM1 formed puncta that clustered near focal adhesions at the trailing edge of migrating cells.
source: Interestingly, we noted that GFP-STIM1 formed puncta that clustered near focal adhesions at the trailing edge of migrating cells (Figure 2; Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Video 3.

claim: Formation of STIM1 puncta is robustly stimulated by thapsigargin.
source: As expected, formation of these puncta, which represent sites of contact between the ER and PM, is robustly stimulated by thapsigargin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: STIM1 puncta formation occurs similarly in cells depleted of either Arf5 or IQSec1.
source: Importantly, this occurs similarly in cells depleted of either Arf5 or IQSec1, indicating that STIM1/Orai1 act upstream of IQSec1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: STIM1/Orai1 act upstream of IQSec1.
source: Importantly, this occurs similarly in cells depleted of either Arf5 or IQSec1, indicating that STIM1/Orai1 act upstream of IQSec1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that STIM1 recruitment is not affected by Arf5 or IQSec1 depletion.

claim: ORP3 co-precipitates with IQSec1 from lysates of co-transfected cells.
source: We first confirmed by immunoblotting that ORP3 co-precipitates with IQSec1 from lysates of co-transfected cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Silencing of ORP3 in MDA-MB-231 cells phenocopied knockdowns of IQSec1 and of Arf5, leading to flattened cells with enlarged focal adhesions.
source: Importantly, silencing of ORP3 in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3B–C) or HT-1080 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) phenocopied knockdowns of IQSec1 and of Arf5, leading to flattened cells with enlarged focal adhesions and a reduced rate of FA turnover (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B-E.

claim: Silencing of ORP3 leads to a reduced rate of FA turnover.
source: Importantly, silencing of ORP3 in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3B–C) or HT-1080 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) phenocopied knockdowns of IQSec1 and of Arf5, leading to flattened cells with enlarged focal adhesions and a reduced rate of FA turnover (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3D-E.

claim: Cells depleted of ORP3 were dramatically inhibited in their ability to migrate in 3D through Matrigel in the transwell migration assay.
source: Moreover, like IQSec1-depleted cells, cells depleted of ORP3 were dramatically inhibited in their ability to migrate in 3D through Matrigel in the transwell migration assay (Figure 3F) and from spheroids embedded in collagen gels (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Cells depleted of ORP3 were dramatically inhibited in their ability to migrate from spheroids embedded in collagen gels.
source: Moreover, like IQSec1-depleted cells, cells depleted of ORP3 were dramatically inhibited in their ability to migrate in 3D through Matrigel in the transwell migration assay (Figure 3F) and from spheroids embedded in collagen gels (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: GFP-ORP3 forms puncta clustered in retractions where focal adhesion disassembly occurs.
source: Intriguingly, live imaging of MDA-MB-231 cells expressing GFP-ORP3 revealed that it formed puncta clustered in retractions where focal adhesion disassembly occurs, and often in close apposition to paxillin-labeled adhesions prior to disassembly (Figure 3H–J, Video 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3H-J and Video 4.

claim: ORP3 puncta are often in close apposition to paxillin-labeled adhesions prior to disassembly.
source: Intriguingly, live imaging of MDA-MB-231 cells expressing GFP-ORP3 revealed that it formed puncta clustered in retractions where focal adhesion disassembly occurs, and often in close apposition to paxillin-labeled adhesions prior to disassembly (Figure 3H–J, Video 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3H-J and Video 4.

claim: ORP3 puncta are enriched in retracting regions of cells.
source: Quantitation of ORP3 localization confirmed that ORP3 puncta were enriched in retracting regions of cells (Figure 3I)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Nearly 100% of disassembling adhesions contained adjacent ORP3 puncta.
source: and that nearly 100% of disassembling adhesions contained adjacent ORP3 puncta, while only ~25% of newly formed adhesions in protrusions did so (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Only ~25% of newly formed adhesions in protrusions contained adjacent ORP3 puncta.
source: and that nearly 100% of disassembling adhesions contained adjacent ORP3 puncta, while only ~25% of newly formed adhesions in protrusions did so (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: ORP3 colocalizes robustly with STIM1 at ER/PM contact sites.
source: Surprisingly, we found that ORP3 not only forms ER/PM contacts but that it also colocalizes robustly with STIM1 at these sites (Figure 4A–B, Video 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A-B and Video 5.

claim: Treatment of cells with thapsigargin led to a dramatic increase in the number and intensity of ORP3 puncta that localized at contacts all over the ventral surface.
source: However, treatment of cells with thapsigargin led to a dramatic increase in the number and intensity of ORP3 puncta that localized at contacts all over the ventral surface, often in linear arrays.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The intensity of ORP3 puncta reached a peak at ~4.5 min after thapsigargin stimulation and declined over time.
source: The intensity of these puncta reached a peak at ~4.5 min after stimulation and declined over time (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4C-D.

claim: Colocalization of ORP3 with STIM1 increased after thapsigargin treatment.
source: Colocalization of ORP3 with STIM1 also increased, (Figure 4A–B), as well as with another marker of ER/PM contacts, the extended synaptotagmin E-Syt1 (Giordano et al., 2013; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A-B.

claim: ORP3 colocalizes with E-Syt1 after thapsigargin treatment.
source: Colocalization of ORP3 with STIM1 also increased, (Figure 4A–B), as well as with another marker of ER/PM contacts, the extended synaptotagmin E-Syt1 (Giordano et al., 2013; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment of cells with the Orai1 blocker BTP2 led to a significant loss of PM puncta and a redistribution of ORP3 to the cytoplasm.
source: In contrast, treatment of cells with the Orai1 blocker BTP2 or knockdown of STIM1 led to a significant loss of PM puncta and a redistribution of ORP3 to the cytoplasm, indicating that recruitment of ORP3 to the PM requires calcium, even at steady state (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4E-G.

claim: Knockdown of STIM1 led to a significant loss of PM puncta and a redistribution of ORP3 to the cytoplasm.
source: In contrast, treatment of cells with the Orai1 blocker BTP2 or knockdown of STIM1 led to a significant loss of PM puncta and a redistribution of ORP3 to the cytoplasm, indicating that recruitment of ORP3 to the PM requires calcium, even at steady state (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4E-G.

claim: Recruitment of ORP3 to the PM requires calcium, even at steady state.
source: In contrast, treatment of cells with the Orai1 blocker BTP2 or knockdown of STIM1 led to a significant loss of PM puncta and a redistribution of ORP3 to the cytoplasm, indicating that recruitment of ORP3 to the PM requires calcium, even at steady state (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that blocking calcium influx or depleting STIM1 prevents ORP3 recruitment.

claim: Treating cells with EGF resulted in the co-recruitment of ORP3 and STIM1 to the PM.
source: Treating cells with EGF, which elevates intracellular calcium through activation of PLCγ, also resulted in the co-recruitment of ORP3 and STIM1 to the PM, albeit more slowly and less dramatically compared to thapsigargin treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and B').
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and B'.

claim: A moderate basal level of association between ORP3 and IQSec1 is significantly increased upon treatment of cells with thapsigargin.
source: As shown in Figure 4H and I, a moderate basal level of association is significantly increased upon treatment of cells with thapsigargin.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4H-I.

claim: Co-precipitation of ORP3 and IQSec1 is reduced in cells pretreated with BTP2.
source: In contrast, co-precipitation is reduced in cells pretreated with BTP2.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The interaction between ORP3 and IQSec1 is modulated by intracellular calcium.
source: Together, these data suggest that the interaction between ORP3 and IQSec1 is modulated by intracellular calcium.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing calcium-dependent changes in ORP3-IQSec1 interaction.

claim: The ORP3 PH-domain is required for recruitment to the PM in response to thapsigargin.
source: In agreement with that earlier study, we found that the ORP3 PH-domain is required for recruitment to the PM in response to thapsigargin (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ORP3 recruitment to the PM was not sensitive to the PI3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin.
source: However, recruitment was not sensitive to the PI3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin, indicating that 3-phosphorylated phosphoinositides are not essential for PM targeting (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: 3-phosphorylated phosphoinositides are not essential for ORP3 PM targeting.
source: However, recruitment was not sensitive to the PI3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin, indicating that 3-phosphorylated phosphoinositides are not essential for PM targeting (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that wortmannin does not affect ORP3 recruitment.

claim: Depletion of PM-associated PI4P using the PI4KIIIα inhibitor GSK-A1 did not impair formation of ORP3 puncta in response to thapsigargin treatment.
source: Depletion of PM-associated PI4P using the PI4KIIIα inhibitor GSK-A1 (Bojjireddy et al., 2014) also did not impair formation of ORP3 puncta in response to thapsigargin treatment (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), indicating that recruitment is not dependent upon PI4P.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: ORP3 recruitment is not dependent upon PI4P.
source: Depletion of PM-associated PI4P using the PI4KIIIα inhibitor GSK-A1 (Bojjireddy et al., 2014) also did not impair formation of ORP3 puncta in response to thapsigargin treatment (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), indicating that recruitment is not dependent upon PI4P.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that PI4P depletion does not affect ORP3 recruitment.

claim: Depletion of PI4P with GSK-A1 did not impair the thapsigargin induced recruitment of ORP3ΔORD.
source: Additionally, depletion of PI4P with GSK-A1 did not impair the thapsigargin induced recruitment of ORP3ΔORD, a mutant lacking the ORD domain (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1F), indicating that lipid binding by the ORD domain is not essential for membrane targeting.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Lipid binding by the ORD domain is not essential for ORP3 membrane targeting.
source: Additionally, depletion of PI4P with GSK-A1 did not impair the thapsigargin induced recruitment of ORP3ΔORD, a mutant lacking the ORD domain (Figure 5 - Figure 4—figure supplement 1F), indicating that lipid binding by the ORD domain is not essential for membrane targeting.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that ORP3ΔORD is still recruited to the PM.

claim: ORP3 recruitment was dramatically inhibited by optogenetic depletion of plasma membrane PI(4,5)P2.
source: In contrast, we found that ORP3 recruitment was dramatically inhibited by optogenetic depletion of plasma membrane PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: Incubation with PMA resulted in rapid recruitment of ORP3 to PM puncta in control cells.
source: As expected, incubation with PMA resulted in rapid recruitment of ORP3 to PM puncta in control cells (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: Optogenetic depletion of PI(4,5)P2 dramatically inhibited the recruitment of ORP3 to the PM after PMA treatment.
source: In contrast, optogenetic depletion of PI(4,5)P2 dramatically inhibited the recruitment of ORP3 to the PM (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: Optogenetic depletion of PI(4,5)P2 resulted in an increase in focal adhesion size.
source: Interestingly, optogenetic depletion of PI(4,5)P2 also resulted in an increase in focal adhesion size (Figure 5C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The recruitment of ORP3 to the PM is mediated by the association of its PH domain with PI(4,5)P2.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the recruitment of ORP3 to the PM is mediated by the association of its PH domain with PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings showing the requirement of the PH domain and PI(4,5)P2 for ORP3 recruitment.

claim: ORP3 was robustly recruited to PM puncta in IQSec1- or Arf5-depleted cells.
source: Surprisingly, we found that ORP3 was robustly recruited to PM puncta in IQSec1- or Arf5-depleted cells (Figure 5D and E), indicating that Arf5 is not essential for ORP3 recruitment to the PM.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5D-E.

claim: Arf5 is not essential for ORP3 recruitment to the PM.
source: Surprisingly, we found that ORP3 was robustly recruited to PM puncta in IQSec1- or Arf5-depleted cells (Figure 5D and E), indicating that Arf5 is not essential for ORP3 recruitment to the PM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that ORP3 recruitment occurs even when Arf5 is depleted.

claim: Silencing of ORP3 led to a > 50% reduction in Arf5 activity.
source: As shown in Figure 5F, silencing of ORP3 led to a > 50% reduction in Arf5 activity (quantified in Figure 5G), indicating that ORP3 is an important regulator of IQSec1 catalytic activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5F-G.

claim: ORP3 is an important regulator of IQSec1 catalytic activity.
source: As shown in Figure 5F, silencing of ORP3 led to a > 50% reduction in Arf5 activity (quantified in Figure 5G), indicating that ORP3 is an important regulator of IQSec1 catalytic activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that ORP3 depletion reduces Arf5 activity.

claim: The ORP3 binding site on IQSec1 is contained entirely within the unstructured loop (residues 152–212).
source: This analysis indicated that the ORP3 binding site is contained entirely within the unstructured loop (residues 152–212), as a mutant lacking this sequence fails to precipitate ORP3 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neither an N-terminal fragment comprising roughly the N-terminal half of ORP3 (1–445) nor an overlapping fragment comprising the C-terminal half (398-886) co-precipitated with IQSec1.
source: Interestingly, neither an N-terminal fragment comprising roughly the N-terminal half of ORP3 (1–445) nor an overlapping fragment comprising the C-terminal half (398-886) co-precipitated with IQSec1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Extending the N-terminal construct to include the second FFAT motif (1-555) yielded a robust interaction with IQSec1.
source: However, extending the N-terminal construct to include the second FFAT motif (1-555) yielded a robust interaction with IQSec1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that the region encompassing this motif (161-454) mediates the interaction of ORP3 with IQSec1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The region encompassing the second FFAT motif (161-454) mediates the interaction of ORP3 with IQSec1.
source: However, extending the N-terminal construct to include the second FFAT motif (1-555) yielded a robust interaction with IQSec1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that the region encompassing this motif (161-454) mediates the interaction of ORP3 with IQSec1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that including the second FFAT motif restores binding.

claim: Deletion of both FFAT motifs in full-length ORP3 resulted in reduced, but still detectable interaction with IQSec1.
source: Deletion of both FFAT motifs in full-length ORP3 resulted in reduced, but still detectable interaction with IQSec1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that these motifs may contribute to, but are not essential, for binding.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: FFAT motifs may contribute to, but are not essential for, ORP3 binding to IQSec1.
source: Deletion of both FFAT motifs in full-length ORP3 resulted in reduced, but still detectable interaction with IQSec1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that these motifs may contribute to, but are not essential, for binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that FFAT deletion reduces but does not eliminate binding.

claim: VAP-A co-precipitates with ORP3 and IQSec1.
source: Instead, we observed that VAP-A co-precipitates with ORP3 and IQSec1, and that increasing amounts of exogenous VAP-A actually enhanced co-precipitation of ORP3, suggesting that the three proteins form a complex in a cooperative manner (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: Increasing amounts of exogenous VAP-A enhanced co-precipitation of ORP3 with IQSec1.
source: Instead, we observed that VAP-A co-precipitates with ORP3 and IQSec1, and that increasing amounts of exogenous VAP-A actually enhanced co-precipitation of ORP3, suggesting that the three proteins form a complex in a cooperative manner (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: ORP3, VAP-A and IQSec1 form a complex in a cooperative manner.
source: Instead, we observed that VAP-A co-precipitates with ORP3 and IQSec1, and that increasing amounts of exogenous VAP-A actually enhanced co-precipitation of ORP3, suggesting that the three proteins form a complex in a cooperative manner (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that VAP-A enhances ORP3-IQSec1 interaction.

claim: Both the calcium ionophore A23187 and the PKC activator phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) induce a phosphorylation-dependent mobility shift in ORP3 on SDS-PAGE gels.
source: Previous studies have shown that both the calcium ionophore A23187 and the PKC activator phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) induce a phosphorylation-dependent mobility shift in ORP3 on SDS-PAGE gels, and that phosphorylation is important for the interaction of ORP3 with VAP-A (Weber-Boyvat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Phosphorylation is important for the interaction of ORP3 with VAP-A.
source: Previous studies have shown that both the calcium ionophore A23187 and the PKC activator phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) induce a phosphorylation-dependent mobility shift in ORP3 on SDS-PAGE gels, and that phosphorylation is important for the interaction of ORP3 with VAP-A (Weber-Boyvat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Pretreatment with Gö6983 potently inhibited Ca2+-stimulated recruitment of ORP3 to the PM.
source: As expected, in control cells thapsigargin stimulated rapid and robust recruitment of ORP3 to the PM (Figure 6A–B). In contrast, pretreatment with Gö6983 potently inhibited Ca2+-stimulated recruitment, indicating that it is indeed dependent on PKC (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A-B.

claim: Ca2+-stimulated recruitment of ORP3 to the PM is dependent on PKC.
source: As expected, in control cells thapsigargin stimulated rapid and robust recruitment of ORP3 to the PM (Figure 6A–B). In contrast, pretreatment with Gö6983 potently inhibited Ca2+-stimulated recruitment, indicating that it is indeed dependent on PKC (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings showing that PKC inhibition blocks ORP3 recruitment.

claim: Treatment with Gö6983 increased focal adhesion size.
source: Interestingly, treatment with Gö6983 also increased focal adhesion size, phenocopying ORP3, IQSec1 and Arf5 knockdowns (Figure 6C—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Treating cells with PMA increased the phosphorylated pool of ORP3.
source: Treating cells with PMA increased the phosphorylated pool of ORP3 (as indicated by a change in mobility of the green band, Figure 6D) and also stimulated the association of ORP3 with IQSec1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Treating cells with PMA stimulated the association of ORP3 with IQSec1.
source: Treating cells with PMA increased the phosphorylated pool of ORP3 (as indicated by a change in mobility of the green band, Figure 6D) and also stimulated the association of ORP3 with IQSec1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Incubation with Gö6983 reduced interaction of ORP3 with IQSec1.
source: In contrast, incubation with Gö6983 reduced interaction of ORP3 with IQSec1 (Figure 6D–E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6D-E.

claim: No ORP3 was precipitated by GST alone under either condition.
